spas.title: Bullfrog A7D
spas.image_alt: Bullfrog A7D hot tub seen from above, shell and JetPaks visible
spas.excerpt: Seven seats, two of them lounges, and the full JetPak wall — the A Series in its most useful size.
spas.overview: The A7D is the model most Eugene and Bend customers end up in. Two lounges and five bucket seats fit a family without pushing the footprint past a standard deck bay, and every seat backs onto a JetPak you can lift out and swap for a different massage in about a minute. The shell is insulated for an Oregon winter and the cover seals against the lip rather than sitting on it.

spas.title: Bullfrog M6
spas.image_alt: Bullfrog M6 hot tub seen from above, six bucket seats around the shell
spas.excerpt: Six bucket seats, three of them elevated, in the smallest M Series footprint we stock.
spas.overview: The M6 is the M Series for a smaller yard. Six bucket seats, no lounge, three of them raised so shoulders sit above the waterline — which is the seat most people actually want on a cold night. Two 2-speed therapy pumps, a dedicated circulation pump and the flat Simplicity filter, so the water turns over without the main pumps running.

spas.title: Bullfrog M9
spas.image_alt: Bullfrog M9 hot tub seen from above, nine seats including two lounges
spas.excerpt: Nine seats, three pumps and 474 gallons — the largest hot tub on either floor.
spas.overview: Nine seats, two of them full lounges, and enough water that the temperature barely moves when four people climb in. Three high-performance 2-speed pumps drive up to 288 jets, and six M Series JetPaks come as standard. It needs a properly poured pad and a 50 amp circuit, and it is worth both.

spas.title: Bullfrog X7
spas.image_alt: Bullfrog X7 hot tub in snow, seen from above with the cover off
spas.excerpt: Eight seats and 395 gallons at the friendliest price we can put a full-size spa on.
spas.overview: The X Series drops the JetPak wall and keeps the shell, the insulation and the pumps. The X7 seats eight around a simple open layout, holds 395 gallons and weighs 661 lbs dry, which makes it the easiest full-size spa we sell to get through a side gate. Choice standard jets, premium exterior sconces and a full jet count.

spas.title: Bullfrog X6L
spas.image_alt: Bullfrog X6L hot tub in snow, seen from above, lounge seat at one end
spas.excerpt: Six seats with a proper lounge, and a footprint that fits a small deck.
spas.overview: Same construction as the X7 in a shorter shell, with one full-length lounge at the far end. Six seats, 350 gallons and a dry weight under 650 lbs. If the space you have is a corner of a deck rather than a patio, this is usually the model that fits without rebuilding anything.

spas.title: Bullfrog STIL 7
spas.image_alt: Bullfrog STIL 7 hot tub seen from above, flush square cabinet
spas.excerpt: A flush square cabinet and a low profile, for a yard where the spa should not shout.
spas.overview: STIL is the design line: a square cabinet, a low 2′9″ profile and hardware hidden behind flush panels. Seven seats, no lounge, and the same JetPak wall as the A Series. It is the model architects specify and the one that looks least like a hot tub when the cover is on.

spas.title: Bullfrog Calm 7
spas.image_alt: Bullfrog Calm 7 hot tub seen from above
spas.excerpt: One pump, seven seats, and the lowest running cost of anything we stock.
spas.overview: Calm is the entry line and the one we recommend to people who want a hot tub rather than a therapy suite. Seven seats, a single pump, 340 gallons and the same cover and insulation as the models above it — which is where the running cost actually comes from. Plugs into a dedicated 240V circuit like the rest.

spas.title: Bullfrog S150 Swim Spa
spas.image_alt: Bullfrog S150 swim spa seen from above, swim area at one end
spas.excerpt: Thirteen seats, a splash pad and a swim current, in the shortest swim spa shell.
spas.overview: At 12′8″ the S150 is the swim spa that still fits a normal back yard. Thirteen seating positions including one exercise seat, a 14-jet splash pad for small children and two swim jets for a current you can work against. 1,190 gallons, so plan the pad before delivery day.

spas.title: Bullfrog S180XD Swim Spa
spas.image_alt: Bullfrog S180XD swim spa seen from above, deep swim channel
spas.excerpt: A 60-inch deep channel and three pumps: the training model, not the party model.
spas.overview: The XD is five feet deep, which is what separates a swim spa you can actually train in from one you tread water in. Three 2-speed pumps, two propulsion jets and 1,856 gallons at fill line. Five seats, because the water in this one is for swimming.

spas.title: Bullfrog S200 Swim Spa
spas.image_alt: Bullfrog S200 swim spa seen from above, seventeen feet long
spas.excerpt: Seventeen feet, 1,950 gallons, and a hot tub end you can heat separately.
spas.overview: The S200 is the full-length swim spa: seventeen feet of channel, nine seats including two lounges, and 1,950 gallons. Swim at one end, soak at the other. It needs a poured pad, a crane or a clear run for the delivery cart, and a conversation with your electrician before you order.
